category-motivation-behavioral-readiness.reason: The exposure-side evidence concerns social-interaction and entertainment motives associated with incidental political-news exposure on social media. The outcome-side evidence concerns motivation to engage in effortful processing associated with recall of political-candidate information. These are motivations for different actions and do not, without further evidence, support a single common confounder inference.
category-motivation-behavioral-readiness.exposure_examples: Motivation for social interaction and motivation for entertainment are linked to incidental exposure to political information on social media.
category-motivation-behavioral-readiness.outcome_examples: Motivation to engage in effortful processing is linked to recall of information about political candidates.
category-motivation-behavioral-readiness.why_not_confounder: Both links involve motivation, but the exposure-side motives concern social or entertainment goals that accompany incidental media contact, whereas the outcome-side motive concerns readiness to process information effortfully. The findings do not establish that the same underlying readiness causes both exposure to news and factual political knowledge.
category-motivation-behavioral-readiness.new_group_rationale: Separate group: social or entertainment motives for media use. It coherently captures the exposure-side reasons for incidental political-news contact, without implying that these motives are equivalent to motivation to process political information effortfully.
category-motivation-behavioral-readiness.residual_group_rationale: Residual group: motivation for effortful information processing and recall. It coherently captures readiness to undertake the cognitive processing behavior linked to factual recall, distinct from motives for social interaction or entertainment.
category-motivation-behavioral-readiness.boundary_cases: Some respondents may use media socially or for entertainment and also be motivated to process political information. Political interest may proxy some news-seeking or processing motivation, but it does not establish that these motives are the same construct; the evidence does not resolve overlap or how either motive relates to event-specific knowledge.

category-personality.reason: The exposure evidence concerns authoritarian personality, whereas the outcome evidence concerns neuroticism, narcissism, and shyness. These are all personality constructs, but they are distinct dispositions and do not establish that a common underlying personality dimension affects both news exposure and factual knowledge.
category-personality.exposure_examples: Authoritarian personality is linked to exposure to partisan media in a US population. This is a politically oriented disposition and a specific form of news exposure.
category-personality.outcome_examples: Neuroticism and narcissism are linked to political knowledge in broad samples or among individuals. Shyness is linked to political knowledge in US introductory-government students, but that finding is excluded as population- and context-mismatched.
category-personality.why_not_confounder: The evidence on the exposure link is specifically about authoritarian personality, while the retained outcome-link evidence concerns neuroticism and narcissism. These constructs are not interchangeable indicators of one common trait, so the combined findings do not establish a single personality confounder affecting both exposure and outcome.
category-personality.new_group_rationale: A group focused on authoritarian or politically oriented personality dispositions is coherent for the exposure link because authoritarian personality may be associated with selecting or encountering partisan media. The evidence does not show that this same disposition predicts factual political knowledge.
category-personality.residual_group_rationale: The residual group of other personality dispositions, such as neuroticism and narcissism, is distinct from authoritarian personality and has evidence on the knowledge link, but no retained evidence here connecting those traits to news exposure. The shyness finding remains excluded.
category-personality.boundary_cases: Authoritarianism can be classified as a personality trait or a political-ideological disposition; here it is grouped with politically oriented personality because the finding concerns partisan-media exposure. Neuroticism and narcissism remain general personality traits. The evidence is limited, and the findings do not establish whether any of these traits share mechanisms or predict both links.
